answers.value: Dheera Shankarabharanam is the Carnatic raga corresponding to Hindustani Bilawal
answers.reasoning: Bilawal is the Hindustani scale of all shuddha (natural) swaras, i.e. the natural major scale; its Carnatic counterpart is the 29th melakarta, Dheera Shankarabharanam, which uses exactly the same seven natural notes. The other three map elsewhere: Nat Bhairavi (20th melakarta) corresponds to Hindustani Asavari, Hanumatodi (8th) to Hindustani Bhairavi, and Kamavardhini or Pantuvarali (51st) to Puriya Dhanashri/Poorvi.

answers.value: The overvalued 1s 6d rupee was fixed to ease the sterling cost of remittances out of India and to protect India's standing as a borrower in London
answers.reasoning: The Hilton-Young Commission fixed the rupee at 1s 6d rather than the 1s 4d Indian opinion demanded. An artificially high rupee meant that fewer rupees were needed to buy the sterling required for the Home Charges, pensions and the repatriated profits of British firms, and it kept India's credit good in the London money market. Option C is the opposite of the effect, since an overvalued currency makes exports such as cotton dearer abroad; option B is a side-effect that the British would not have adopted the policy for. RUNNER-UP: D. The Commission did also recommend a gold bullion standard, so a reviewer who reads the item as asking about the monetary-standard rationale rather than the fiscal one would pick D; D would win if the question is about why the rate was pegged at all rather than why it was pegged high.

answers.value: The Pali coin-names plus the punch-marked silver coins are evidence for both the rise of towns and the shift to a money economy
answers.reasoning: The Pali references to kahapana, nikkha, kamsa and kakanika, corroborated by large finds of silver punch-marked coins, are the standard evidence for the monetisation of exchange in the sixth-to-fourth centuries BC. Coinage is also one of the defining markers of the second urbanisation of the middle Ganga plain, because regular coined money presupposes the specialised craft production, market exchange and trade on which the new towns rested. RUNNER-UP: B. If the examiner reads the coin evidence narrowly, as speaking only to how exchange was conducted and not to where people lived, then 2 alone follows and B wins; C requires accepting coinage as an indirect indicator of urbanism, which is the usual textbook treatment.

answers.value: Huchimalligudi at Aihole and the Dashavatara temple at Deogarh have Nagara shikharas; Malegitti Shivalaya and Virupaksha are Dravida
answers.reasoning: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh is a Gupta-period shrine carrying one of the earliest surviving curvilinear Nagara towers. The Huchimalligudi at Aihole is the early Chalukyan experiment with the northern rekha-prasada shikhara, and is cited precisely for introducing that form in the Deccan. By contrast the Malegitti Shivalaya at Badami and the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal, the latter modelled on the Kailasanatha at Kanchipuram, are both Dravida vimanas with stepped, storeyed superstructures.

answers.value: Yaksha is not one of the four Jaina gatis; the four are deva, manushya, tiryancha and naraki
answers.reasoning: Jaina cosmology divides all embodied existence into four gatis or states of birth: deva (heavenly beings), manushya (humans), tiryancha (animals and plants) and naraki (hell beings). Yakshas are attendant demi-gods who appear in Jaina iconography as shasanadevatas beside the Tirthankaras, but they fall within the deva category and are not a separate form of existence.

answers.value: The Hallisalasya panel at Bagh depicts a group folk dance
answers.reasoning: The best-known paintings of the Bagh caves are in Cave 4, the Rang Mahal, whose celebrated panel shows a band of dancers and musicians. Hallisa or hallisaka is a circular group dance performed by women, and lasya is its graceful mode; the panel is therefore identified as a joyous folk dance scene, not a devotional or narrative subject. Buddha in meditation, Shiva and Parvati on Kailasa, and the churning of the ocean are all subjects of other sites.

answers.value: All three statements about the spread of place-value notation are correct
answers.reasoning: The earliest dated Indian epigraphic use of decimal place-value numerals is the Gujarat copper-plate grant of AD 595-96, dated in year 346 of the Chedi era. Place-value numerals become general in Indian inscriptions from the ninth century, the Gwalior inscription of AD 876 with its zero being the classic instance. And Sanskrit inscriptions in South-east Asia carry place-value numerals from the seventh century, the Cambodian and Old Malay records of AD 683 being the earliest known. RUNNER-UP: C. Statement 1 is the only one that could fail, and only on the naming: if the examiner treats the AD 595 grant as the Sankheda plate and holds the Mankani plates to be a different record, statement 1 becomes false and C wins.

answers.value: Inferences 1 and 2 follow; inference 3 does not, because private wells and bathing platforms indicate private rather than common property
answers.reasoning: Spindle-whorls scattered through the houses with no spinning wheels show that thread was drawn by hand-spindle inside the home, which is slow and laborious work, so inference 1 follows from statement I. Graduated scales and a standardised system of weights are a genuine achievement in measurement, so inference 2 follows from statement II. Inference 3 is the reverse of what statement III says: houses with their own wells, their own bathing platforms and large private courtyards point to individual household property and to differences of wealth, not to a common property system.

answers.value: Bardoli was against a land-revenue enhancement while the Eka movement was against excessive rents
answers.reasoning: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928, led by Vallabhbhai Patel in Surat district, was a refusal to pay a steep enhancement of the land-revenue assessment. The Eka or unity movement of 1921-22 in the Awadh districts of Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur and Barabanki was a protest by tenants against rents pitched far above the recorded rates and against oppression by thikadars. A is wrong because the Congress withdrew from Eka, whose leadership passed to Madari Pasi, while Bardoli was a Congress-led campaign from the start; B is wrong because Eka was directed against the taluqdars and Bardoli was a movement of peasant proprietors, not landless labourers; D misplaces both, since Eka was in Awadh and Bardoli in south Gujarat, not Saurashtra.

answers.value: Only the pulley-and-pail evidence and the pre-Rigvedic use of the ox support the claims about well irrigation and animal-drawn water-lifting
answers.reasoning: The two assertions are specifically that wells extended cultivation away from the flood plains, and that draught animals were used to raise the water. Item 1, the ashma chakra or stone pulley wheel and the ahava or strapped pails, is the direct technological evidence for lifting water from a well, and supports both. Item 3, the use of the ox before the Rigveda for ploughing and drawing carts, establishes that the draught-animal power assumed in the second assertion was already available. Item 2 concerns axes and sickles, which belong to forest clearance and harvesting and say nothing about wells or about lifting water, so it supports neither assertion.

answers.value: The shared dolphin species in the Indus and Ganga systems is the basis for inferring a Pleistocene connection between them
answers.reasoning: The assertion is about the Pleistocene, a geological epoch many millennia before any Indian text, so the Nadi-sukta of the Rigveda cannot be evidence for it; the Rigvedic river list bears on the second millennium BC at the earliest. The biogeographical argument is what does the work: the occurrence of the same river dolphin in both the Indus and the Ganga drainages is hard to explain unless the two systems were once joined, which is exactly the kind of tributary transfer the assertion describes. Robert Bruce Foote was a geologist of Indian prehistory whose fieldwork lay mainly in the peninsula, not in a survey of the Sutlej and the Yamuna. RUNNER-UP: C. C would win if the examiner intends the assertion to rest on textual and survey evidence rather than on biogeography, treating the dolphin point as a modern aside; the Pleistocene dating in the stem is what argues against that.

answers.value: The empty seat stands for the Buddha's meditation
answers.reasoning: Early Buddhist art at Bharhut and Sanchi is aniconic and represents the Buddha through symbols rather than a human figure. Each symbol carries a fixed reference: the wheel stands for the first sermon at Sarnath, the stupa for the mahaparinibbana, the riderless horse for the great departure, the Bodhi tree for the enlightenment, and the empty seat or vacant throne for the Buddha's meditation.

answers.value: Only Parushni-Ravi is correct; Vitasta is the Jhelum, Asikni the Chenab, and the Beas is the Vipasha, not the Yavyavati
answers.reasoning: The standard Rigvedic identifications are Vitasta with the Jhelum and Asikni with the Chenab, so pairs 1 and 2 have simply been exchanged. Parushni is the Ravi, on whose banks the Battle of the Ten Kings was fought, so pair 3 is right. The Beas is the Vipasha or Vipas; Yavyavati is a much less certainly located stream and is not the Beas, so pair 4 fails. Only 3 stands.

answers.value: Amaravati stood in the lower Krishna valley and its sculpture shaped later South Indian and overseas art, but it was not smaller than Sanchi
answers.reasoning: Amaravati lies on the Krishna in Guntur district, in the lower reaches of the valley, so statement 1 is correct. The Amaravati school did have a long afterlife, in later South Indian sculpture and in images carried to Sri Lanka and South-east Asia, so statement 3 is correct. Statement 2 fails on measurement: the Amaravati Mahachaitya, at roughly fifty metres across, was larger than the Great Stupa at Sanchi, which is about thirty-seven metres, so Amaravati was not next after Sanchi in size. RUNNER-UP: D. D would win if the source the paper is drawn from states the Sanchi comparison in those words; a text that ranks Amaravati second to Sanchi in importance rather than in size would produce exactly this statement.

answers.value: Only pair 2 is wrong: Udiyanjeral was a Chera, not a Chola
answers.reasoning: Udiyanjeral, or Perunjeral Adan, is the Chera king of Sangam tradition celebrated for feeding both armies at Kurukshetra, so pairing him with the Cholas is incorrect. The other two are right: Senguttuvan is the Chera of the Silappadikaram who founded the Pattini cult, and Nedunjeliyan is the Pandya of Talaiyalanganam. The question asks which pairs are NOT correctly matched, so the answer is 2 only.

answers.value: Gandhi's loss of confidence, the disunity of the Congress Left, and the preference of the Royists and Jayaprakash Narayan for Congress unity drove Bose to form the Forward Bloc
answers.reasoning: Bose won the presidency at Tripuri in 1939 against Gandhi's candidate but could not carry Gandhi with him, and the Pant resolution then required him to nominate a Working Committee in accordance with Gandhi's wishes; his resignation and the founding of the Forward Bloc in May 1939 followed directly. The decisive weakness was that the Left was fragmented rather than behind him: M.N. Roy's followers opposed him outright and Jayaprakash Narayan's Congress Socialists stayed neutral, both in the name of preserving Congress unity. RUNNER-UP: A. Statement 3 is the pivot. The Communists deserted Bose at Tripuri, which makes it look true, but they had backed his candidature against Pattabhi Sitaramayya only weeks earlier, so a blanket claim that they did not support him is questionable; A wins if the examiner reads statement 3 as referring only to Tripuri and afterwards.

answers.value: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; the taluqdars were disarmed and their forts destroyed, so statement 1 is wrong
answers.reasoning: After the annexation of 1856 the taluqdars were not left in possession of their arms: their forts were demolished and their armed retainers disbanded, which is why statement 1 fails. The Summary Settlement of 1856 did proceed on the assumption that the taluqdars were interlopers with no permanent stake in the soil, who had established their hold by force and fraud, so statement 2 is correct. And the object of removing them was precisely to settle the revenue directly with the actual cultivating proprietors, which the British expected would both raise revenue and reduce the exploitation of peasants, so statement 3 is correct.

answers.value: All three statements support the claim that community-based political alliances grew out of the design of the 1919 reforms
answers.reasoning: The Montagu-Chelmsford scheme did not merely keep the separate electorates conceded in 1909 but widened them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans, so statement 1 shows the communal principle written into the reforms themselves. Statement 2 supplies the intent behind that design, that separate representation was meant to blunt a nationalism the British found increasingly hard to contain, which is what makes the divisiveness inherent rather than accidental. Statement 3 supplies the mechanism by which the design produced alliances, since groups that stood to gain from communal representation organised themselves to claim it. RUNNER-UP: C. Statement 3 is the vulnerable one, because the Depressed Classes were given nominated seats in 1919 and did not receive separate electorates until the Communal Award of 1932; C wins if the examiner reads deprived classes strictly in that sense. A stricter reading still, that only statement 1 describes the nature of the reforms while 2 is motive and 3 is consequence, would give A.

answers.value: Mallikarjun Mansur sang in the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana
answers.reasoning: Mallikarjun Mansur of Karnataka, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1992, is the best-known twentieth-century exponent of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana, having trained under Manji Khan and then Burji Khan, the sons of Alladiya Khan who founded that gharana. His early training was in the Gwalior style, but his mature style and repertoire of rare ragas belong squarely to Jaipur-Atrauli.

answers.value: The term kshetra-patni, mistress of the field, is traced to the Atharvaveda
answers.reasoning: The Atharvaveda is the Vedic text most concerned with settled agriculture and with the household and its rituals, carrying the ploughing and sowing charms and the invocation of Sita, the personified furrow, so a feminine title for the presiding figure of a field belongs most naturally there. The Rigveda has the masculine kshetrapati, lord of the field, in its hymn to the field-deity, but not the feminine form. NOTE: this rests on a recalled attribution I am not certain of rather than on anything derivable from the stem, hence the low confidence. RUNNER-UP: C. The Ashtadhyayi is the text historians most often mine for socio-economic vocabulary of this kind, and Panini's rules on forming feminines in -patni would account for the word directly, so C wins if the paper is drawing on the Paninian evidence for women holding land. A is a weaker third: the Rigveda would win only if the examiner is treating the Kshetrapati hymn as also yielding the feminine.

answers.value: Relationships 1 and 2 hold: the BUR-4 emission-decline data empirically supports the LT-LEDS claim, and the short-termism of statement III contradicts the long-horizon approach implicit in statement I
answers.reasoning: Statement I is factually correct — India's Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy, submitted at COP27 in 2022, is the framework document for the net-zero-by-2070 pledge. Statement II is also factually correct: the Fourth Biennial Update Report submitted in December 2024 reported roughly a 7.93 per cent fall in greenhouse gas emissions in 2020 relative to 2019. Relationship 2 is the clearest of the three: statement III insists that climate-resilient development 'necessarily depends on quick and short-term' emission cuts, which is exactly the opposite of the long-term, phased transition that a 2070 net-zero strategy is built on, so III does contradict the approach implicit in I. Relationship 3 fails on the same ground — a statement that contradicts I cannot 'together with I' establish a premise of long-term sustainability. Relationship 1 is the judgement call and is the reason this is MED: the 2020 fall is very largely a COVID-19 lockdown artefact and predates the LT-LEDS itself by two years, so a strict reader could say it supplies no empirical support for I at all. However the option set contains no '2 only', so relationship 1 must be accepted for any option to be defensible, and read loosely — declining measured emissions being evidence that the stated pathway is credible — it does support I. RUNNER-UP: A (1 only), which would win if a marker held that III merely places a different emphasis rather than contradicting I. Note that had the setter intended '2 only', the item would be defective as printed.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; gibbons are small, light apes and have nothing of the heavy gorilla build asserted in statement 3
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary in Jorhat district, Assam, is the flagship protected area for the Western Hoolock Gibbon, which the IUCN Red List classifies as Endangered. Statement 2 is correct and is the defining locomotor trait of the family — gibbons are the specialist brachiators among apes, with elongated forelimbs and hook-like hands that let them swing hand-over-hand through the canopy. Statement 3 is false: the Western Hoolock Gibbon is a small ape weighing roughly 6 to 9 kg, and its light frame is precisely what makes brachiation possible; a gorilla-like heavy build would be incompatible with the arboreal swinging described in statement 2, so statements 2 and 3 cannot both be true.

answers.value: Only statement 3 is a valid rationale — mangroves act as natural bio-shields against tidal surges and as a biomass-based livelihood base
answers.reasoning: Statement 3 is the standard climate-resilience case for mangroves: their dense stilt-root systems dissipate wave and cyclone-surge energy, earning them the description 'bio-shield', while fuelwood, honey, fodder and fisheries make them a livelihood base for coastal communities. Statement 1 is wrong on two counts — mangroves do not store freshwater, and converting them to paddy is a recognised cause of mangrove loss, not a reason to protect them. Statement 2 inverts the biology: mangrove roots are salt-tolerant, excluding or excreting salt rather than being 'salt-sensitive', and clearing mangroves for aquaculture ponds is one of the largest global drivers of mangrove destruction. Both 1 and 2 describe the conversion of mangroves to other land uses, which is the opposite of a rationale for protecting them.

answers.value: Only statement 3 is correct — Vizhinjam's natural deep draft and location near the east-west shipping lane let India retain trans-shipment cargo that previously went to foreign ports
answers.reasoning: Vizhinjam is India's first dedicated deep-water container trans-shipment port: a natural draft of about 20 metres needing minimal dredging, sited roughly 10 nautical miles from the main east-west shipping channel, so it can handle the largest mother vessels. Its strategic point is precisely that about three-quarters of India's trans-shipment cargo had been handled at Colombo, Singapore and Salalah, and Vizhinjam is intended to retain that traffic and the associated revenue in India — exactly statement 3. Statement 1 is false in every clause: the port is built for international trans-shipment, not domestic cargo alone, and it was developed in partnership with a private developer using foreign-supplied equipment. Statement 2 is false: it is a container port, not a cruise-tourism or heritage-shipping project.

answers.value: The Sutlej — it is antecedent, rises on the Tibetan Plateau, crosses China, India and Pakistan, is a major irrigation river, and being a tributary of the Indus it never builds distributaries
answers.reasoning: All four clues have to be satisfied together, and clue 4 is what decides the item. The Sutlej rises near Rakas Lake close to Mansarovar on the Tibetan Plateau, cuts a deep antecedent gorge across the Himalaya, flows through China (Tibet), India and Pakistan, and feeds the Bhakra-Nangal system and the canal network of Punjab and Rajasthan; because it is a tributary that merges into the Indus through the Panjnad, it never reaches the sea and so forms no distributaries. The Indus and the Brahmaputra each satisfy the first three clues — both are classic antecedent rivers rising on the Tibetan Plateau and each crosses three countries — but both build large deltas with well-developed distributaries, so both fail clue 4. The Teesta fails clue 2, flowing through only India and Bangladesh.

answers.value: Statements 2 and 3 are the incorrect ones — West Bengal, not Rajasthan, has the longest international border among States, and Meghalaya also touches only one other State
answers.reasoning: The question asks which statements are NOT correct. Statement 1 is correct, so it is not part of the answer: Uttar Pradesh borders eight States — Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Bihar — more than any other State (Assam is next with seven). Statement 2 is incorrect: Rajasthan has the longest border with Pakistan, about 1,070 km, but the longest international border of any Indian State belongs to West Bengal, which shares roughly 2,217 km with Bangladesh besides its frontiers with Nepal and Bhutan. Statement 3 is incorrect: Sikkim indeed touches only West Bengal, but Meghalaya likewise touches only Assam among Indian States, so Sikkim is not the only such State.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct — the Doyang Lake story is a community-conservation success; tracking technology does not guide the birds, and the falcons remain passage migrants
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct and is the whole significance of the Doyang episode: villages around the reservoir, notably Pangti, turned from mass trapping of the falcons in 2012 to organised protection, and Nagaland is now described as the Amur Falcon capital of the world. Statement 2 is false as worded — satellite transmitters fitted to individual falcons allow researchers to observe the migration route; they play no part in guiding the birds, whose navigation is innate. Statement 3 is false: the Amur Falcon is a passage migrant that halts at Doyang for a few weeks to fatten before the non-stop crossing of the Arabian Sea to southern Africa; there is no permanent resident population in India.

answers.value: Only statement 3 is an RAD objective — raising productivity and reducing climatic risk through Integrated Farming Systems
answers.reasoning: Rainfed Area Development is the component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture built around the Integrated Farming System, which combines crops with horticulture, livestock, fishery, apiculture and agro-forestry so that a farmer's income does not collapse when a single crop fails — exactly statement 3. Statement 1 is the opposite of the scheme's logic: RAD promotes diversification, and monoculture is precisely the vulnerability it is designed to reduce. Statement 2 is out of scope twice over, since RAD targets rainfed and not irrigated areas, and promoting more rice in irrigated regions belongs to a different policy stream altogether.

answers.value: Both statements are correct — Oeko-Tex certification of Eri silk both opens high-end chemical-free markets and formally attests conformity with international standards for premium eco-conscious buyers
answers.reasoning: The two statements are two faces of the same implication. Oeko-Tex certification tests textiles against a harmful-substances list, and for Assam's Eri silk it supplies the third-party attestation that European and other premium buyers demand — so statement 1 follows directly, since exporters can now bid for high-end segments that require chemical-free assurance, and statement 2 states the same result in the language of formal conformity that opens eco-conscious markets. The near-duplication of the two statements is itself a signal that both are intended to be accepted. RUNNER-UP: A (1 only). It would win if the marker read statement 2 strictly, because the Oeko-Tex Standard 100 label certifies freedom from harmful substances for human-ecological safety and does not, by itself, certify 'quality' or environmental performance — those belong to the separate STeP and Made in Green schemes. If that strictness is applied, statement 2 overreaches and only statement 1 survives.

answers.value: Bahrain and Qatar — both lie inside the Persian Gulf, so their shipping must pass the Strait of Hormuz to reach the Indian Ocean
answers.reasoning: The Strait of Hormuz is the only sea outlet of the Persian Gulf, connecting it through the Gulf of Oman to the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean. Bahrain is an island State within the Persian Gulf and Qatar is a peninsula projecting into it, so vessels from both must transit Hormuz. Syria has no Persian Gulf frontage at all; its ports at Latakia and Tartus are on the Mediterranean, and its shipping would reach the Indian Ocean through the Suez Canal and the Red Sea. Egypt likewise fronts the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, reaching the Indian Ocean via Bab-el-Mandeb, never through Hormuz.

answers.value: Ecuador — Tungurahua is an Andean stratovolcano in central Ecuador near Banos, and its surroundings form the Tungurahua Volcano UNESCO Global Geopark
answers.reasoning: Tungurahua is a well-known active stratovolcano of the Ecuadorian Andes, rising above the town of Banos de Agua Santa in Tungurahua province, and its eruptive episodes from 1999 onward are among the most closely monitored in South America. The volcano's location fixes the answer independently of the Geopark designation: the peak and the province of the same name lie wholly in Ecuador, so Peru, Bolivia and Colombia are excluded on geography alone.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — Madhav National Park became a Tiger Reserve in 2025 and contains the Ramsar-listed Sakhya Sagar, but it lies wholly within Madhya Pradesh
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: Madhav National Park in Shivpuri district was notified in March 2025 as India's 58th Tiger Reserve and Madhya Pradesh's ninth. Statement 2 is correct: Sakhya Sagar, a lake created on the Manier river in the 1920s, lies inside the park and was designated a Ramsar Site of international importance in 2022. Statement 3 is false: the park is situated entirely in Shivpuri district of Madhya Pradesh and shares no part of its area with Rajasthan.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; December to May is the islands' dry season, not the period of maximum precipitation
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct — the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have a warm, humid, tropical coastal climate with a small annual temperature range moderated by the surrounding sea. Statement 2 is correct and is the islands' distinctive feature: they receive rain from the south-west monsoon between about May and September and again from the retreating north-east monsoon between about November and December, giving them a long wet season. Statement 3 is false and in fact reverses the picture: December to May is the relatively dry part of the year on the islands, with rainfall building from May onward and peaking during the monsoon months.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are Peninsular features; deep V-shaped valleys cut by fast-flowing rivers belong to the young Himalayan mountains, not to the Peninsular Block
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Peninsula has stood as a rigid block since the Cambrian, the recognised exception being part of its western coast, which is submerged beneath the sea, and other parts altered by tectonic movement and block faulting. Statement 2 is correct: the Peninsula's relief is dominated by worn-down residual mountains, the standard examples being the Aravali hills, the Nallamala hills, the Javadi hills, the Veliconda hills, the Palkonda range and the Mahendragiri hills. Statement 3 is false for the Peninsular Block: its rivers are graded, near base level and flow in broad, shallow valleys, whereas deep V-shaped valleys and gorges cut by swift, actively downcutting rivers are the signature of the youthful Himalayan region. Since statement 2 is certainly correct and statement 3 certainly incorrect, only an option pairing them without 3 can stand.

answers.value: Relationships 1 and 2 hold: the growth and ranking data validate the port-led strategy, and Sagarmala 2.0 extends that strategy into a future-oriented innovation framework
answers.reasoning: Statement I states the core Sagarmala aim of port-led development through cost-effective, sustainable coastal infrastructure; statement II reports outcomes — growth in coastal and inland waterway traffic and better global port rankings — which is exactly the kind of evidence that validates the strategy in I, so relationship 1 holds. Statement III describes Sagarmala 2.0 carrying the same port-led logic forward into a maritime innovation agenda tied to Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047, which extends rather than displaces the objectives in I, so relationship 2 holds. Relationship 3 fails because statement I is not confined to traditional infrastructure and nothing in it is inconsistent with the modernisation described in III; an extension is not a contradiction, so relationships 2 and 3 cannot both be true.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — the Foxtail orchid is epiphytic and is the State flower of both Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, but it is not endemic to North-east India
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is certainly correct: Rhynchostylis retusa grows as an epiphyte on tree trunks and branches, drawing moisture from the air through aerial roots rather than rooting in soil. Statement 2 is certainly false: the species is distributed widely across tropical and sub-tropical Asia, from India, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bhutan through Myanmar, Thailand and Indo-China to Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines, so it is not endemic to North-east India. Statement 3 is the pivot: Rhynchostylis retusa is the State flower of Assam, where it is the Kopou phul of Bihu songs, and it is also recorded as the State flower of Arunachal Pradesh, which makes the statement correct as printed. RUNNER-UP: A (1 only). It would win if Arunachal Pradesh's State flower is in fact some other orchid, since statement 3 claims both States and a single wrong State makes it false; this item rests on a recalled State-symbol fact rather than on anything in the stem, which is why it is not marked HIGH.

answers.value: Only statement 3 — the Moidams are the burial mounds of Ahom royalty and nobility at Charaideo
answers.reasoning: The Moidams of Charaideo in Assam, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2024, are the vaulted burial mounds in which the Ahom kings and nobles were interred with their possessions, a mound-burial tradition the Tai-Ahoms carried into the Brahmaputra valley and maintained for some six centuries. They served no military or recreational purpose, so statements 1, 2 and 4 — fortresses, recreation centres and battle-drill grounds — are all false, leaving statement 3 alone.

answers.value: Better production, better nutrition, better environment and better life — the four aspirations of FAO's Strategic Framework, applied to Blue Transformation
answers.reasoning: The 'Four Betters' are the aspirations set out in FAO's Strategic Framework 2022-31 for transforming agri-food systems: better production, better nutrition, a better environment and a better life, the last carrying the leave-no-one-behind commitment. Blue Transformation is FAO's programme for applying that same framework to aquatic food systems through sustainable aquaculture, effective fisheries management and upgraded value chains, so it inherits the four aspirations unchanged. Options A, C and D each swap one of the four for an ocean-specific item — better ocean, better coral reefs, better estuaries, better mangrove vegetation — none of which belongs to the Four Betters.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 only — Lake Turkana is the world's largest desert lake and a World Heritage Site nicknamed the Jade Sea, but it lies in Kenya and Ethiopia, not South Sudan
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: Lake Turkana is the largest permanent desert lake in the world and also the largest alkaline lake. Statement 3 is correct: the Lake Turkana National Parks, comprising Sibiloi National Park and the South and Central Island parks, are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, and the lake's algae-tinted colour has earned it the name Jade Sea.
